caption: A hand squeezes a wet kitchen sponge over a sink, water streams out, and the sponge springs back to shape when the hand opens.

sa.check: A wet kitchen sponge is held in a hand over a sink.
The hand squeezes and the sponge compresses.
Water comes out of the sponge.
The hand opens and the sponge returns toward its shape.
A sink is below the sponge.
The order is squeeze, water out, release, spring back.

pc.expect: The sponge compresses only where and while it is squeezed and expands again when the grip opens, recovering most of its shape.
pc.fail: The sponge stays crushed after the hand opens; or it expands while the hand is still closed on it; or it compresses before the fingers close; or it behaves as a rigid block that does not compress.

pc.expect: Water leaves the sponge during the squeeze and runs down into the sink; the sponge does not take water back in from the air.
pc.fail: Water streams out while the sponge is unsqueezed; or water rises from the sink back into the sponge; or the sponge grows wetter as it is squeezed.

pc.expect: The released water falls straight down into the sink.
pc.fail: Water floats away from the sponge; or flows sideways or upward; or hangs beneath the sponge without falling.

pc.expect: The expelled water behaves as a liquid: a stream or drips that splash and spread in the sink.
pc.fail: The water comes out as solid lumps; or as balls that bounce off the sink like rubber; or it keeps a fixed shape after leaving the sponge.

pc.expect: One hand with its fingers and one sponge keep their number and identity; the hand does not pass through the sponge.
pc.fail: Fingers multiply, vanish or pass through the sponge; or the sponge splits in two or merges with the hand; or water appears away from the sponge or vanishes in mid-air.

pc.expect: The sponge keeps its colours and the sink stays the same.
pc.fail: The sponge changes colour or its scouring side swaps; or the sink's contents change between frames.
